The supplied corpus is the only literature context available here, so novelty relative to other literature remains unresolved.", "Abstract": "Spatial coarsening is an established conclusion of the source study. A distinct follow-up question is whether the shear observable tracks the instantaneous spatial correlation width, or retains information about the recent coarsening path. We hypothesize conditionally that, at the same width, mean shear may differ depending on whether width has recently been increasing or decreasing. This would be consistent with a lagged response or hysteresis, but could also arise from a shared time trend, smoothing, or measurement noise. We will analyze only the supplied 2,199-sample experimental aggregate, treating samples as a serial time series rather than independent replicates. After checking sampling regularity and plotting both observables, we will compare a baseline smooth model of shear from width and time against a model that additionally includes a prespecified lagged width change and its interaction with width-growth direction. We will test robustness across reasonable smoothing windows and lag choices, using blocked time-series validation and block-bootstrap uncertainty rather than row-wise random splits. The conditional prediction is that the lag term improves held-out prediction and the estimated shear difference between growth and decline remains directionally stable at matched widths. If this pattern vanishes after controlling for time or is unstable to analysis choices, the memory hypothesis is unsupported by this export. Even a robust association would motivate, not prove, a dynamical mechanism: the aggregate lacks repeated-run identifiers, raw image sequences, and independently characterized uncertainty. The result would be a careful hypothesis-generating test and a concrete specification for future controlled experiments.", "Experiments": ["Load measurements.csv, verify columns, row count, time ordering, missing values, and duplicate timestamps.
